title: GA launch criteria + beta exit checklist — Hosted canary rollouts
creator: Paula Mendes
sub_issues: Create GA go/no-go doc + signoff list (Console/Platform/SRE/Security/Support)
Confirm default auto-stop thresholds by tier/region for GA
Finalize customer-facing limitations/known issues section for docs
Support macros + troubleshooting flow for auto-pause / split mismatch
Run GA staging game day with stop/rollback + audit validation
description:
Purpose
- Define the Beta Exit criteria and GA Launch checklist for the Hosted canary rollout workflow (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes).
- Align Console, Control Plane, Smart Routing/Data Plane, Telemetry/SRE, Security, Docs, and Support on what “GA-ready” means.
- Serve as the single checklist for the GA go/no-go meeting and as a record of what we validated.

Scope reminder (GA)
- Hosted routes only (Dedicated/Private: schema-compatible, not GA)
- Console wizard to create/run/pause/rollback, plus timeline/activity view and cohort comparison metrics
- Policy guardrails: max step size, min soak time, approval gates (RBAC), auto-stop/auto-rollback based on SLO metrics
- Audit logging + customer-visible activity timeline

Beta Exit Criteria (must meet before scheduling GA)
1) Design partner validation
- Minimum: 5 design partners enabled, with at least 3 running a real production canary on Hosted.
- At least 10 completed rollouts end-to-end (create → start → step changes → reach 100% OR rollback).
- No P0/P1 issues open related to incorrect routing split, inability to rollback, or audit trail gaps.
- Qualitative: partners confirm they can understand (a) current step, (b) what will happen next, (c) why auto-stop occurred, and (d) how to rollback.

2) Reliability outcomes during beta
- No unresolved incidents attributable to rollout feature causing widespread request misrouting or outages.
- Any beta incidents have documented root cause, fix merged, and backported as needed (e.g., metric timeout stall bugfix; split mismatch learnings).
- SRE signoff that alerts are actionable and not generating sustained alert storms.

3) Governance + safety outcomes during beta
- Policy guardrails enforced consistently across UI and API (no bypass via API for restricted actions).
- Approval gates tested with RBAC role(s) (rollout-approver) and common enterprise setups.
- Audit events present for all required action types, with correct actor identity and diffs.

GA Launch Checklist (go/no-go)
A) Functional completeness (Console + API)
Owner: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Wizard flow supports:
  - Selecting route, baseline model version/config, canary model version/config
  - Defining traffic schedule (step %, soak duration)
  - Configuring guardrails (max step size, min soak time) and showing validation errors clearly
  - Review + confirm with explicit warnings for destructive actions (rollback)
- Lifecycle actions supported and validated end-to-end:
  - Create rollout (draft)
  - Start rollout
  - Progress to next step (with/without approval gate)
  - Pause/resume
  - Rollback (manual) and “rollback to baseline” semantics
  - Auto-pause / auto-rollback on SLO breach (with reason surfaced)
- State machine correctness:
  - No “stuck” states on metric evaluation timeouts; clear retry + user-facing error
  - Idempotent retries for control plane → data plane propagation
- API parity for core operations (documented): create, get status, list activity, approve step, pause/resume, rollback

Acceptance evidence
- E2E test suite passing in CI and nightly (ENG-9164)
- Staging manual walkthrough recorded (link in go/no-go notes)

B) Smart Routing enforcement correctness
Owner: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Deterministic cohorting implemented and documented (hash inputs + stickiness rules)
- Percentage split accuracy within tolerance per region (define tolerance below)
- Correct behavior for:
  - Multi-region traffic
  - Streaming requests
  - Retries (client and internal)
  - Fallback routing interactions (baseline vs canary; precedence per ADR)
- Kill switch behavior verified:
  - Tenant-level disable immediately forces 100% baseline
  - Global disable forces baseline and prevents new rollouts from starting

Split accuracy target (GA)
- For stable traffic volume, measured canary proportion should converge to target within ±2% absolute over a 15-minute window (per region), excluding low-volume routes.
- For low volume routes, UI must display “insufficient volume” guidance instead of implying precise percentages.

Acceptance evidence
- Staging smoke tests (perf-canary PR-147)
- Post-fix validation for beta split mismatch scenario (see incident thread: rollout-split-mismatch-us-east)

C) Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting
Owner: Sean Gallagher / Aisha Bello / Logan Wright
Required cohort signals (tagging + aggregation)
- Every request must be attributable to:
  - route
  - model version/config (baseline vs canary)
  - cohort (baseline/canary)
  - region
  - rollout_id (with cardinality controls; ensure no blowups)
- Metrics required in Console comparison view + internal dashboards:
  - Request rate (RPS)
  - Error rate (overall, 5xx, timeouts)
  - Latency (p50/p95; ideally p99 in internal)
  - Tokens/sec and cost proxies (where available)
  - Streaming-specific failure modes (disconnects, partial completions) if tracked

Stop conditions (GA defaults)
- Auto-stop/auto-rollback must be available and enabled by default for new rollouts (with ability to tune thresholds by entitlement/tier).
- Default thresholds (initial GA proposal; finalize with SRE):
  - 5xx error rate: canary exceeds baseline by +1.0% absolute AND exceeds 2.0% absolute for 5 minutes
  - Timeout rate: canary exceeds baseline by +0.5% absolute for 5 minutes
  - p95 latency regression: canary p95 > baseline p95 * 1.25 for 10 minutes (guard for low volume)
- Rollout behavior on breach:
  - Auto-pause first if we can attribute breach confidently; auto-rollback when breach persists (or per policy)
  - Always emit: (1) customer-visible timeline entry, (2) audit event, (3) notification event

Alerting guidelines
- Alerts should page SRE only for:
  - Routing enforcement drift/incorrectness
  - Orchestrator stuck rollouts at scale
  - Global cohort tagging failures
  - Control plane → data plane propagation failures
- Customer route-specific canary SLO breaches should notify customer in Console/timeline and optionally via webhook/email (no paging unless systemic).

Acceptance evidence
- Cohort dashboards exist + validated against known traffic patterns (PR-28910 / observability pack PR-184)
- Cardinality analysis completed and within limits (Drive: rollout-cohort-metrics-cardinality-analysis)

D) Audit logging + change history (Security/Compliance)
Owner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei
Required audit event coverage
- Events must be emitted for:
  - rollout.created
  - rollout.started
  - rollout.step.approval_requested
  - rollout.step.approved / rollout.step.denied
  - rollout.step.changed (percent change)
  - rollout.paused / rollout.resumed
  - rollout.rolled_back (manual)
  - rollout.auto_paused / rollout.auto_rolled_back (include stop condition + metric snapshot reference)
  - rollout.completed
- Required fields (high level): tenant_id, actor_id/actor_type, route_id, rollout_id, previous_state → new_state, diff (human readable + structured), timestamp, request_id/trace_id when applicable.
- Retention and export:
  - Align with existing audit log retention policy by tier
  - Verify SIEM export compatibility (field naming and size limits)

Customer-visible activity timeline
- Must match audit events but may exclude security-only internal fields; should show “what happened” and “why” (e.g., auto-pause reason).

Acceptance evidence
- Security review of audit event schema doc (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)
- Sample events captured in staging and validated by Security (screenshots/log dumps referenced in go/no-go)

E) Policy guardrails + RBAC
Owner: Jordan Lee / Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Guardrails enforced for step changes:
  - Max step size (e.g., 1% → 50% disallowed without override/approval)
  - Minimum soak time before next step
  - Approval gates configurable by tenant/admin policy
- Entitlement mapping documented:
  - Which customers get auto-rollback, approvals, advanced retention, etc.
- RBAC roles validated:
  - Who can create rollouts
  - Who can start/pause/rollback
  - Who can approve (rollout-approver role)
- UI error messaging must reflect policy engine errors with actionable guidance (e.g., “Wait 20m more to satisfy min soak”)

Acceptance evidence
- Policy engine tests and Console integration tests pass (PR-28802)
- Manual validation with at least 2 common enterprise role setups

F) Documentation (public + internal)
Owner: Elliot Price / Wei Chen
Customer docs must include
- Conceptual overview: baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time
- Step-by-step Console walkthrough
- API reference (or links) for rollout operations
- Troubleshooting:
  - Why a rollout auto-paused
  - Why metrics show “insufficient volume”
  - Split mismatch debugging steps (what to check before contacting support)
  - How to rollback safely
- Limitations (GA):
  - No bandits/dynamic optimization
  - Quality gates optional/manual (not hard gates)
  - Dedicated/Private not GA

Internal docs must include
- Enablement how-to (feature flags, permissions, sanity checks)
- On-call runbook for stuck rollout / bad split
- Release/change management checklist

Acceptance evidence
- Docs PR merged (redwood-docs PR-922)
- Runbooks published (Confluence) and reviewed with SRE + Support

G) Support readiness + incident response
Owner: Dev Patel / Rafael Mendes
- Support playbooks:
  - Triage flow for “rollout paused unexpectedly after latency spike”
  - Triage flow for “traffic split not matching config”
  - Escalation path to on-call / engineering
  - What data to request: tenant_id, route, rollout_id, timeframe, region, request IDs
- Macros/snippets created for common questions (e.g., “How do I do a percentage rollout on Hosted route?”)
- SLA for response during GA launch week and ownership for escalation channel

Acceptance evidence
- At least 2 support training sessions run (recording link in go/no-go)
- Sample tickets resolved using new macros (reference: SUP-48211, SUP-48302, SUP-48377)

H) Release management + staged rollout plan
Owner: Connor O'Brien / Soojin Lee
- Feature flags:
  - Per-tenant enablement
  - Internal dogfood tenants first
  - Staged cohort of beta → expanded beta → GA default (if applicable)
  - Kill switch playbook (owners + steps)
- Migration/backward compatibility validated for config schema changes
- Backout strategy:
  - Disable canary UI
  - Force baseline routing
  - Preserve audit logs and rollout history for completed rollouts

Acceptance evidence
- Change management checklist completed (Drive: hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist)
- Release readiness review held 48–72 hours pre-GA

Go/No-Go Process (how we decide)
Meeting: GA Readiness Review (60 minutes)
Required attendees / signoffs
- Product: Marissa Cole (final call)
- Console Eng: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Platform/Policy: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee
- Smart Routing: Mina Haddad
- SRE: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes
- Security: Marcus Lin
- Docs/Support: Elliot Price + Dev Patel

Decision rules
- No-go if any of:
  - Known issue causing incorrect split enforcement at material rates
  - Rollback unavailable or unreliable
  - Missing audit events for any action type listed above
  - Unbounded metrics cardinality risk unresolved
  - No validated kill switch
- Conditional go allowed if:
  - Minor UI polish issues only
  - Non-blocking docs follow-ups with explicit owner + date
  - Non-paging alert tuning improvements queued (does not impact safety)

Artifacts to attach in go/no-go notes
- Links: PRD, design spec, ADRs
- Latest beta partner tracker snapshot
- List of open bugs (P0/P1 only) with owners + ETA
- Staging game day results + any follow-ups

Current status / open questions (as of last update)
- Need final agreement on GA default thresholds by region/tier; beta feedback suggests p95 multiplier threshold may be too aggressive for long-context routes.
- Confirm whether GA requires customer notifications beyond Console timeline (e.g., webhook). If not in GA, docs must state Console-only.
- Ensure “insufficient volume” guidance text matches design copy and does not confuse customers about split accuracy.
